## Office furniture in Newcastle is usually the last thing you buy — and that's the problem

By the time most Newcastle businesses start looking at office furniture, the money is nearly gone.

The lease is signed. The builder has been paid. The electrician found something no one expected. And furniture — the only part of the office your team actually touches every day — gets whatever is left over.

Think of your office project as a pie. From the day it starts, up to thirty contractors, suppliers and agents need a slice. The ones at the front of the queue take theirs early. Furniture sits at the back. That's why so many offices end up with a beautiful reception and staff sitting on chairs nobody wants to sit in by 3pm.

You can avoid all of that. It just means making a few decisions earlier than feels natural.

Here's what to get right when you're buying office furniture in Newcastle.

## Start with how your team works — not with a catalogue

Every furniture conversation should start with three questions:

- How many people are in the office on a busy day, not on paper?
- How many of them are on video calls, and where do those calls happen?
- What do you want a client to see in the first ten seconds?

The answers change everything. A firm with ten staff and four in the office on any given day doesn't need ten desks — it needs six good ones and a bookable quiet room. A business that hosts clients weekly needs a meeting table that holds up, not a bigger boardroom.

Buying furniture before you've answered those questions is how businesses end up with a storeroom full of monitor arms and nowhere quiet to take a call.

## Measure the space properly before you spend a dollar

A common planning benchmark for professional services is roughly 8–12m² per person once you count desks, meeting rooms, kitchen and circulation space. Newcastle's older Hunter Street stock and the newer Honeysuckle buildings behave very differently against that number — columns, odd floor plates and glazing lines eat more space than people expect.

Two practical things:

1. Get a floor plan with furniture on it before you order anything. Not a mood board — a plan with dimensions.
2. Check the circulation space between workstations. If people have to turn sideways to get past a colleague's chair, it will annoy them every single day for the length of your lease.

## What office furniture actually costs

Indicative commercial ranges for Newcastle, per person, excluding GST:

- Entry level, new commercial grade: around $800–$1,200 (desk, task chair, basic storage)
- Mid range: around $1,500–$2,500 (electric height-adjustable desk, better task chair, personal storage)
- Premium: $3,000+ per person

Meeting rooms, breakout areas, reception and soft seating sit on top of that.

The most common mistake isn't overspending. It's spending evenly. Put the money where people spend hours — chairs and desks — and be sensible everywhere else. A cheap boardroom table gets seen twice a week. A cheap task chair gets felt eight hours a day and costs you in sick leave and grumbling.

*(Pricing is indicative only and depends on specification, volume and lead time — get a scoped quote before you budget.)*

## Australian-made versus imported: it's really a lead time decision

Imported furniture can be sharp on price. It can also sit on a ship while your fit out finishes and your staff work from home for another three weeks.

Australian-made commercial ranges — including the Academy Range manufactured by our supply partner EOF Group in Lambton — generally give you shorter lead times, easier warranty support and the ability to match or add pieces in twelve months when you hire three more people. That last point matters more than people expect. Discontinued imported stock is how offices end up mismatched.

Rule of thumb for Newcastle projects: allow 4–8 weeks from order to install for stocked commercial lines, and longer for custom joinery or made-to-order finishes. If your fit out finishes in three weeks and you haven't ordered furniture, you have a problem right now.

## Ergonomics isn't a nice-to-have — it's a legal duty

Under the *Work Health and Safety Act 2011 (NSW)*, you have a duty to provide a safe working environment. Workstation setup is part of that.

In plain terms, that means:

- Task chairs with proper seat height, depth and lumbar adjustment
- Desks at a height that lets forearms sit level, or height-adjustable desks
- Monitors at eye level — which usually means monitor arms, not a stack of books
- Enough space to move

None of this is expensive when it's specified at the start. All of it is expensive when it's retrofitted after someone lodges a claim.

## Delivery and installation: the part everyone forgets

This is where Newcastle projects come unstuck more often than anywhere else.

Before you order, check:

- **Loading access.** Many Newcastle CBD and Honeysuckle buildings have limited dock access and strict booking windows.
- **Lift dimensions.** A 2400mm boardroom table doesn't care how good it looks in the showroom if it doesn't fit in the lift.
- **Building rules.** Some require after-hours delivery, certificates of currency and an induction before anyone touches a trolley.
- **Rubbish removal.** New furniture arrives in an extraordinary amount of cardboard. Someone has to take it away, and it isn't the building manager.
- **Old furniture.** Decide early whether it's being resold, donated or dumped. Landfill fees and a truck are a real cost.

Ask your supplier what's included. "Delivered" and "delivered, assembled, positioned and rubbish removed" are two very different quotes.

## Why buying office furniture locally in Newcastle is worth it

Newcastle is a relationship market. That's true for commercial property and it's true for furniture.

A local commercial supplier will come and look at your space. They'll hold stock. They'll send someone out when a gas lift fails in month four instead of directing you to an online form. And when you hire two more people next year, they can match what you already own.

Newcastle also has proper commercial suppliers on the ground — including EOF Group in Lambton, who manufacture locally and stock commercial brands including Rapidline, Desky and Sebel. You don't have to buy from Sydney and hope.

## The five mistakes we see most often

1. **Ordering too late.** Furniture lead times get compressed to fit a fit out program that was set months earlier.
2. **Buying residential-grade furniture for a commercial office.** It looks fine for a year, then it doesn't. Commercial warranties exist for a reason.
3. **Buying for today's headcount.** If you're growing, plan the layout for the headcount you'll have when the lease is halfway through.
4. **Ignoring acoustics.** Hard floors, glass and open plan make a room no one can concentrate in. Soft finishes and screens fix it cheaply.
5. **No one owning the process.** Furniture sits between the landlord, the builder, the IT contractor and the supplier. When nobody owns it, it falls through the gap.

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does office furniture cost per person in Newcastle?**

Expect roughly $800–$1,200 per person for entry-level commercial grade, $1,500–$2,500 for mid range with a height-adjustable desk and a good task chair, and $3,000+ for premium. Meeting, breakout and reception areas sit on top.

**How long does office furniture take to arrive?**

Allow 4–8 weeks from order to installation for stocked commercial ranges in Newcastle. Custom joinery and made-to-order finishes take longer. Imported stock can take considerably longer again.

**When should I order office furniture during a fit out?**

As soon as the floor plan is settled — usually well before construction finishes. Ordering at the end of the project is the single most common cause of staff working without desks.

**Can I buy office furniture without an interior designer?**

Yes, for most offices under about 30 people. What you do need is an accurate floor plan, a clear headcount and someone coordinating delivery with the builder and the building manager.

**Do I need height-adjustable desks?**

You're not legally required to provide them, but you are required to provide a safe workstation. Height-adjustable desks make that easier across a team of different heights, and staff value them.

## One conversation, not five

Furniture is one slice of the pie. It works best when the person specifying it also understands the lease you signed, the fit out program, and the building you're moving into.
